lines.scene: Cold open, no fade. One terminal panel centre-frame at 58% width on warm near-black #12100e, lit by a single cyan wash pooling from above — cyan is a light source here and stays one all film. Mono types `rename userSvc -> userService`, then `3 files changed`. Three job labels stack to its right as they are named: `read the repo` / `rename the handler` / `judge the auth boundary`. Behind the panel a grey scrollback column of ~40 dim lines is ALREADY scrolling before the first word. A 1px gold hairline enters from the left edge and stays — the conductor rail, planted at frame one.
lines.animation: Mono types at 16 chars/sec. The three job labels stamp in at unequal stagger 0.11 / 0.17 / 0.24s, each y 10px→0 and opacity 0→1 in 0.25s power2.out. The cyan wash holds at opacity 0.55 and never dims — it is the meter, and it is pinned at full. The grey scrollback translates y 0→-180px over the line, linear, physically pushing its top line out of its own clipped box. The gold hairline draws left→right scaleX 0→1 in 0.8s sine.out.

lines.vo: One chat, one model, every job. That is why the bill is high, and the work gets worse.
lines.scene: The camera pulls back and the panel is suddenly small and alone. Three mono captions stamp to the right: ONE CHAT / ONE MODEL / EVERY JOB. A token tally climbs beside the cyan lamp. The grey scrollback fills the panel from the bottom until only two live lines are left at the top. Deliberately no numbers on the bill yet — the image is the claim.
lines.animation: Container scale 1.0→0.92 over 2.2s sine.inOut. Captions stamp at unequal stagger 0.11 / 0.16 / 0.22, y 8px→0 in 0.22s power2.out. Token tally tweens 0→1,240,000 with GSAP snap:1 over 1.8s. On the second sentence the cyan wash brightens opacity 0.55→0.72 in 0.4s and holds through the gap. The grey column's height tweens 40%→88% over 1.6s power1.in.

lines.vo: You didn't install a tool. You hired a manager. He runs the team. You only talk to him.
lines.scene: The gold hairline at the left thickens and resolves into THE DESK: a brass-railed card, centre-left, the only element in the whole film that ever faces the viewer square-on. The one-chat panel shrinks off-axis right, goes dark, and keeps one dim grey line scrolling as a reminder. `/tyran` draws in mono on the desk. Four steel-railed agent cards fade up behind it at 14%, dark and unlit, in two uneven columns — off-axis, smaller, facing the work rather than the viewer.
lines.animation: Hairline width 1px→3px in 0.3s. The desk's border draws itself via stroke-dashoffset 420→0 in 0.5s power2.inOut. The one-chat panel scales 1→0.42 and moves x +260px with opacity 1→0.35 over 0.7s power3.inOut. `/tyran` types at 14 chars/sec. The four agent cards fade opacity 0→0.14 at unequal stagger 0.13 / 0.19 / 0.16 / 0.22 — never a symmetrical fan.

lines.vo: He interviews you first. At most four questions, each with his recommendation.
lines.scene: The operator's words arrive from off-frame top in the SANS face, gold, unaligned to any grid, carrying a real shadow: `make the settings tab write, without losing my comments`. They land on the desk. Four question rows type in beneath, each with a muted `recommend:` line under it and a corner counter reading `4 / 4`. A fifth row begins to draw, is struck through, and is replaced by the file's own sentence in mono: `"Shall I continue?" is forbidden.  skills/run/SKILL.md`. A hairline tag holds under the batch: `after the plan is accepted: zero questions except at gates`.
lines.animation: The sentence drops y -120px→0 with opacity 0→1 in 0.5s power3.out; on contact the desk's rail flashes --brass-bright for 0.2s and returns. Rows type at 22 chars/sec with unequal stagger 0.13 / 0.19 / 0.16 / 0.14. The fifth row's strike-through draws scaleX 0→1 in 0.3s power2.inOut, then that row fades opacity 1→0 in 0.25s while the file quote fades 0→1 over the same 0.25s — a substitution, not a dissolve. The fourth caret keeps blinking through the gap.

lines.vo: Then he stops asking. The plan becomes tickets, on a board.
lines.scene: The board ARRIVES as one object — it does not fade in. Rebuilt natively at the board's own tokens (bg #1c1a16, hairline #332e27, --brass #a8863c, --steel #7d9ea9, --sage #88a06a, --clay #c07a70). Header: `Tyran board · 3 initiative(s) · 8/17 tickets merged (47%)`. The real five-tab bar sits above it and stays on screen for every board shot in the film: `Overview · Board · Waiting on you (2) · Spend · Settings`. Seven cards fall into BACKLOG carrying real titles — `T-1 — derive lanes from the journal fold`, `T-3 — board.html: self-contained, zero CDNs`, `T-5 — the waiting-on-you queue and the answer sheet`. The desk persists as a 3px brass rail down the left edge of frame.
lines.animation: The whole board rises y +90px→0 with opacity 0.2→1 in 0.55s power3.out — it arrives, the camera does not dissolve to it. Cards drop y -140px→0 with back.out(1.7), 0.5s each, at unequal stagger 0.09 / 0.14 / 0.11 / 0.17 / 0.12 / 0.20 / 0.15. Each landing increments its lane-header count by textContent tween, and the lane border warms --hairline→--brass-edge for 0.25s and returns.

lines.vo: Then the team goes out. A scout reads the repo. Cheap tier, read only.
lines.scene: THE SPLAY. Agent cards are born at the desk's exact rect and travel to steel-railed columns, off-axis, at unequal distances and unequal arrival times. The scout leaves first, lands nearest, and is the smallest card. Its three-line micro-terminal scrolls a fixed, deterministic list: `git log --oneline -20`, `ls scripts/`, `command -v gitleaks`. A cyan lamp above the scout column comes up dim and stays dim. The board holds behind at 10% and keeps ticking.
lines.animation: GSAP fromTo seeded from the desk's own getBoundingClientRect, so the cards visibly come OUT of it: x/y from desk centre to column position, scale 0.35→1 in 0.55s power2.out. The scout's lamp fades opacity 0→0.28 in 0.3s and holds — dim, and on almost continuously. Its micro-terminal steps y by -22px every 0.4s through its three fixed lines. No radial fan, no org chart, no connecting arrows.

lines.vo: Implementers take one story each. Own branch, empty scrollback. The agents forget. The team doesn't.
lines.scene: Two implementer cards land further out, each labelled with its own branch (`T-6/sandbox`, `T-7/spend-ledger`). The point is what is NOT in them: each scrollback panel is EMPTY except a single handoff line, `ticket T-7 · files: scripts/cost.mjs, docs/cost.md`. Beside them the old one-chat grey column rises one last time for contrast and is pushed out of frame for good. Then one mono path draws across the bottom and holds: `.tyran/state/<init>/journal.jsonl · committed to your repo`.
lines.animation: Two cards emitted from the desk rect with unequal travel (280px / 420px) and unequal arrival (0.5s / 0.68s, power2.out). The grey column translates y 0→-260px over 1.1s power1.in with opacity→0. The journal path types at 22 chars/sec. Simultaneously the scout chip collapses scale 1→0.4 and travels BACK along its exact outbound path in 0.6s power2.inOut, landing on the desk, where a sage `+1` fades up on the ledger line — the fold-back, and the first proof that cheap agents finish while the others are still out.

lines.vo: The reviewer grades the diff and cannot edit it. Otherwise it approves its own patch.
lines.scene: The reviewer card arrives last, on the far axis. Its real tool grant types in: `Read  Grep  Glob  Bash  WebFetch  WebSearch`. Then a second row draws — `Edit · Write · NotebookEdit` — and is struck out. No red, no warning icon; the absence is the point. A 1s muted provenance chip fades under it: `agents/reviewer.md`. Two implementer terminals keep scrolling behind, and a lane count ticks at the frame edge.
lines.animation: Card arrives 0.5s power2.out. Tools type at 26 chars/sec. The three editor names fade opacity 0→1, then a 1px rule draws across them scaleX 0→1 in 0.3s power2.inOut and they settle to opacity 0.3. The provenance chip fades 0→0.6→0 across 1.0s. Minimum two motions in flight the whole time — the struck row and the scrolling terminals.

lines.vo: A good manager doesn't put a principal engineer on a grep. Roles resolve to tiers, in one file.
lines.scene: The real routing block types on over the columns, under its own header comment verbatim: `# The ONLY place model names appear.` Then four lines with their true inline comments, the model column MASKED to `····` so the header explains the restraint rather than hiding something: `cheap ···· # scout, mechanical sweeps, ledger bookkeeping` / `work  ···· # DEFAULT: implementation and ordinary review` / `deep  ···· # root-cause diagnosis, hard implementation, risky review` / `top   ···· # security review, arbitration, final acceptance`. Each line lights one lamp on the right. Then the file slides away and only the four lamps remain, running a compressed work cycle, split against a left panel labelled `one chat`. LIGHT IS THE BILL: the Tyran half is visibly darker.
lines.animation: Header comment types at 20 chars/sec, then the four lines at 26 chars/sec, 0.18s apart. As each lands its lamp's cyan opacity rises to its tier level — cheap 0.28, work 0.50, deep 0.70, top 0.90 — in 0.25s power2.out. The YAML then slides x 0→-420px with opacity→0 in 0.4s. Over the next 8 compressed seconds: cheap holds 0.28 almost continuously; work pulses 0.50↔0.30 every 0.6s; deep flares to 0.70 three times for 0.5s each; top flares to 0.90 exactly twice, ~0.9s total, and is dark otherwise. The left panel's single lamp holds 0.95 for the entire cycle while its grey scrollback grows and pushes its useful line out of the box.

lines.vo: Security review always gets the strongest tier. No flag can drop it. No cost setting either.
lines.scene: A terminal on the desk types the real, reproducible command: `node scripts/tiers.mjs --role security-review --tier cheap`. The tool's own stderr prints verbatim — `tiers: override "cheap" RAISED to top/max — "security-review" has a floor that cannot be lowered` — and the camera frames exactly two keys of the JSON, `"tier":"top"` and `"floored":true`, with the rest of the object masked so no model name enters frame. A hairline tag beneath: `the floor is applied last, so it cannot be shifted out of`. This is a command the viewer can paste tonight, not an animation of a promise.
lines.animation: Command types at 20 chars/sec. On ENTER the top lamp dips opacity 0.90→0.72 for 0.18s and SNAPS back to 0.90 in 0.12s power4.out — the escalation the product refuses to allow. The stderr line fades 0→1 in 0.25s. The JSON prints, then a 0.35s power3.inOut snap-to re-centres and scales the block 1→1.35 while every key except those two tweens to opacity 0.25.

lines.vo: All of it lands on one page. Five agents running. Two questions waiting on you.
lines.scene: The camera ARRIVES on the board; it has been live since shot five, so it is not re-introduced. Persistent tab bar with `Waiting on you (2)` planted in it. Four Overview tiles at their real values: WAITING ON YOU 2 / `answer them on the next tab` · AGENTS RUNNING 5 / `across 3 initiative(s)` · PROGRESS 47% / `8 of 17 merged` · NEEDS A HUMAN 4. The agent strip arrives stalest-first beneath, one chip carrying `5 HOURS since last signal — likely dead` in clay.
lines.animation: Tiles count up 0→2, 0→5, 0→47, 0→4 over 0.7s with GSAP snap:1, staggered 0.12 / 0.18 / 0.14. The strip's five chips rise y 14px→0 with opacity 0→1, stagger 0.12, stalest first. Mid-shot one chip's age colour tweens --brass #a8863c → --sage #88a06a over 0.4s because it just signalled — the cheapest possible proof the page is alive. Slow push scale 1.02→1.05 across the whole line, sine.inOut.

lines.vo: That card crossed into done by itself. Nobody dragged it there. This is Tyran, building Tyran.
lines.scene: A lateral pan, no cut — the board stays one continuous object underneath. `T-5 — the waiting-on-you queue and the answer sheet` slides IN-REVIEW → DONE. IN-REVIEW (1) ticks to (0), DONE (8) to (9), and the header re-renders digit by digit from `8/17 tickets merged (47%)` to `9/17 tickets merged (53%)`. Then the three initiative names light in sequence: `the-board · overnight-mode · settings-editor` — the three that actually built this board. There is no cursor graphic anywhere; the state change is the interaction.
lines.animation: Container x 0→-160px over 2.4s sine.inOut. The card tweens one lane width in 0.5s back.out(1.7); its rail warms to --brass for 0.3s then settles --sage. Counts tween with snap:1; the header digits swap on a 0.05s stagger. The three initiative names tween opacity 0.45→1 at unequal stagger 0.16 / 0.22 / 0.13. Elsewhere and unremarked, the blocked lane's clay rail pulses opacity 0.6→1→0.6 once.

lines.vo: Halfway through, you remember something else. So you say it.
lines.scene: The board is already live and already ticking — this beat does not introduce it, it interrupts it. Your words type over the lanes in the SANS face, gold, unaligned to the grid, floating with a real drop shadow and a blinking caret: `also — rate-limit the webhook before we ship`. It must look like it does not belong on the board.
lines.animation: Board wrapper filter brightness 1→0.88 over 0.3s. The sentence types at 15 chars/sec, held at a 2.5° off-grid rotation with a 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.55) shadow. Two unrelated things keep moving underneath: an age chip flips `129 min`→`131 min`, and the in-progress rail pulses once, 0.6→1→0.6.

lines.vo: It doesn't land in the scrollback. It becomes a ticket. Queued as T nine.
lines.scene: THE PEAK, one continuous shot with no cut. The conductor's gold runs along the board's top hairline and strikes the floating sentence. On contact the letterforms snap sans → MONO and snap left onto the grid, and a card border DRAWS itself around them clockwise from the top-left. `T-9` types into the corner. Gravity applies: the card drops into BACKLOG, the lane count ticks (1) → (2), the dim lifts. Half a second later, one muted mono receipt appears under the top hairline — `journal: ticket.declare T-9 · appended` — and fades on its own. That line is why it is un-loseable rather than merely acknowledged. Then it is picked up: the rail turns steel, an agent name types beneath, and the card slides one lane right.
lines.animation: A 3px gold segment travels the top hairline x 0→860px in 0.35s power2.in. On contact: font-family swaps to mono, rotation 2.5°→0, text-align snaps left, all in 0.18s power4.out — mechanical, not magical — landing exactly on the word 'ticket' in the voiceover. The border draws stroke-dashoffset 640→0 clockwise in 0.45s power2.inOut. `T-9` types in 0.2s. The card drops y -220px→0 with back.out(1.7) in 0.5s; the lane border warms --brass-edge for 0.3s and returns; board brightness 0.88→1 in 0.3s. The receipt fades 0→1 in 0.25s, holds 0.9s, fades to 0 in 0.5s. Throughout, at least two unrelated motions continue elsewhere in frame.

lines.vo: A real decision comes back with a recommendation, not a shrug. You answer here, and the run carries on.
lines.scene: A snap-to onto `Waiting on you (2)`; the panel SLIDES under the same persistent tab bar rather than dissolving to a new page. One real question card, rebuilt natively at legible weight, revealed in the order that IS the argument: kind tag `DECISION · A DEFAULT IS RECORDED`, then the question verbatim — `The board reloads itself every 30 seconds, which wipes a half-typed model name. Pause the refresh while the Settings tab is open, or keep the page always-live and accept the loss?` — then `RECOMMENDATION  pause it while Settings is open — the other three tabs stay live, and an unsaved field is the only thing at risk`, then `DEFAULT`, then `BLOCKS 1 ticket(s): T-5`. A caret types a short answer, the Answer button flashes brass, the card collapses to one sage line, and the tab label ticks (2) → (1). Hairline note: `served with --write`.
lines.animation: Snap-to 0.35s power3.inOut. Panel x +80px→0 with opacity 0.3→1 in 0.4s. Card rows reveal top-down, y 8px→0, stagger 0.14. Answer types at 18 chars/sec. Button background tweens --brass-low→--brass and back over 0.2s. Card height tweens to a single line in 0.35s power2.inOut as its rail turns --sage. The tab count swaps 2→1 LAST, and that decrement is the final thing the eye catches before the panel slides away.

lines.vo: Then the bill. Four and a half million tokens. Four hundred and four requests.
lines.scene: The Spend panel slides in under the same tab bar — a native rebuild at board tokens, never a scaled capture. Tiles count up: `TOKENS 4.5 M / 404 requests`, `COST THROUGH THE API $16.97`, `CONDUCTOR OVERHEAD 55% / of tokens, no ticket`. The token count and the dollar figure are always in frame together, and the rate-card caption is never framed close enough to read. The composition bar draws left to right — output 41%, cache read 33%, cache write 19%.
lines.animation: Panel x +80px→0 with opacity 0.3→1 in 0.4s. TOKENS tweens 0→4.5 with one decimal, `404` snaps with snap:1, `$16.97` counts up over 0.8s. Composition bar segments scaleX 0→1 from the left, sequential, 0.35s each power2.out, the 41% output segment first, and the bar stops rather than looping.

lines.vo: Fifty-five percent of those were the manager's own context. It gets its own row, so nothing hides.
lines.scene: The CONDUCTOR OVERHEAD tile pulses once and holds at 55%. Beneath it the by-agent-type rows begin to draw, conductor FIRST at $8.73, rendered in the muted not-a-ticket tone the board itself uses. A hairline connector draws from the tile to that row carrying the board's own sentence: `conductor context is not attributable to any ticket; it is its own row so the rows sum to the total`. Volunteering the least flattering number is the fastest route past 'multi-agent burns more tokens'.
lines.animation: Tile border tweens --hairline→--brass and back over 0.5s. The conductor bar scaleX 0→1 in 0.5s power2.out. A 1px connector draws scaleX 0→1 in 0.3s power2.inOut, then the sentence fades 0→0.85 in 0.3s and holds. Nothing in this shot takes gold — gold stays reserved for the operator's own queue.

lines.vo: The scout's whole reconnaissance cost three cents. This is not an estimate. It is the bill.
lines.scene: The remaining rows draw in descending order at their real values — implementer $6.72, reviewer $1.48, then scout $0.03, a sliver three pixels wide. The camera holds on the scout row while every other bar stays drawn: the arithmetic is left to the viewer and no savings figure is spoken or drawn anywhere. Rows are labelled by ROLE only. Then the TOKENS | COST toggle visibly flips and every label re-renders — a toggle that works on camera is proof of a live page. Drawn beneath, never spoken, the repo's own doctrine: `Tokens are facts, money is an opinion.`
lines.animation: Bars scaleX 0→1 from the left at unequal stagger 0.22 / 0.16 / 0.28, 0.45s each power2.out. The camera holds 1.6s on the scout row while its label tweens --muted→--brass in 0.3s. The toggle's active pill slides x 0→-64px in 0.25s power3.inOut and every numeric label cross-fades to its token value over 0.3s. The doctrine line fades 0→0.8 in 0.4s.

lines.vo: None of this is a prompt asking nicely. A hook decides, before the tool runs.
lines.scene: A terminal panel rises over the board, which keeps ticking behind it at 30%. Show what is in danger FIRST: a diff of three ordinary files, and a fourth line carrying `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA••••••••••••`, elided on screen exactly as the gate elides it — a refusal must never republish the secret. Then `git commit -m "wire up the uploader"` types itself. It is an ordinary, well-intentioned command, and that is the point.
lines.animation: Panel rises y +120px→0 with opacity 0→1 in 0.45s power3.out. Diff lines fade in at stagger 0.09. The key line's background lifts to --gold-low for 0.4s then settles back. The command types at 18 chars/sec while the desk's brass rail thickens 3px→6px across the caret's path over 0.3s — the stop is being built before it is needed.

lines.vo: A commit carrying a secret is refused. Even inside a markdown file.
lines.scene: The caret hits the brass rail and the command block recoils once. One `REFUSED` tag in clay for well under a second; the refusal body in muted text ending `(4812 bytes, coverage verified)`. Then the beat ENDS ON THE PASS: the line becomes `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${env}`, the command re-runs, and `EXIT=0` prints in sage. Drawn under the passed commit, the gate's own stated limit: `not a guarantee — a mechanical check at the point the damage becomes permanent`. Red is the verdict; gold is what the shot is left holding.
lines.animation: The command block tweens x 0→-6px→0 in 0.12s power4.out, ONCE — no shake loop, no error iconography. The REFUSED tag fades 0→1 in 0.1s, holds 0.6s, out in 0.2s. The refusal body types at 30 chars/sec. The key line cross-fades to `${env}` in 0.15s, the command re-types at 24 chars/sec, and `EXIT=0` fades up in --sage over 0.25s. The frame's accent settles from clay back to brass across 0.4s.

lines.vo: A report with no command output is refused too. It blocks silence, not forgery.
lines.scene: The same rhythm, faster, so the rhythm itself becomes legible as 'this is what a gate does'. A report reading `Ran the suite — everything is green. Typecheck is clean.` recoils against the same brass rail. The refusal's first line prints verbatim: `REFUSED by the tyran evidence gate: this report carries no raw command output.` The report comes back carrying `# pass 343  # fail 0` and goes through in sage. Behind it, on the native board, the `Errors logged (2)` row lights brass for a beat — the refusal has somewhere to be logged, and this is it.
lines.animation: The identical 0.12s power4.out recoil, played at 1.4× the previous speed. The refusal line types at 40 chars/sec. The report block cross-fades to its evidence-bearing version in 0.25s and its rail tweens --clay→--sage over 0.3s. Behind, the board's `Errors logged (2)` row tweens border-colour --hairline→--brass and back over 0.6s. The concession line `it blocks silence, not forgery` holds at opacity 0.7 through the gap.

lines.vo: You try to close the session. It refuses. Once. The team runs the retrospective on itself.
lines.scene: Back to the desk — the spine closing. Every ticket of the initiative comes home as sage-railed cards and compresses into one line: `initiative closed · 7 tickets · 4 agents`. The closing line types, and the Stop hook refuses it exactly once, in muted text with exactly one clay word: `tyran: initiative "the-board" has all 7 of its tickets merged and no retrospective recorded since the last merge.` Then the retro agent spawns LAST, after everything else has already come home, and it READS rather than writes.
lines.animation: The done cards travel back along their own outbound paths in 0.7s power2.inOut and collapse into a single line via a height tween in 0.3s power2.inOut. The refusal types at 42 chars/sec. A cyan scan-line — a CSS linear-gradient band, 120px tall — sweeps a tall thin column of mono journal lines from y -100% to +100% over 1.2s, linear. Light moving over text; nothing is written yet.

lines.vo: One lesson is promoted. One is rejected. One is retired. Work you keep asking for becomes a skill.
lines.scene: Three fates resolve at three different moments in ONE frame, because a promotion without a visible rejection reads as bloat. (a) A candidate rises and HARDENS into the knowledge panel — sans becoming mono — gaining the id `K-12` and an `applies_to` glob. (b) A second meets four small gates, `recurs? · cost measured? · already covered? · one sentence?`, fails on the third, and drops out of frame. (c) An existing rule carrying `helped 0 / 6` is struck through and slides out. The panel ends holding the same number of rows it started with. Then the fourth fate: three identical asks in the journal light in sequence, compress into one card that hardens into `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and that skill name appears in the roster behind the desk — the manager hiring a specialist.
lines.animation: Candidate A: y +30px→0 with a font-family swap and a border drawing stroke-dashoffset 480→0 in 0.4s power2.inOut. Candidate B: its four gates light 0.18s apart, the third flashing --clay for 0.35s, then B tweens filter grayscale 0→1 and y 0→+140px with opacity→0 over 0.5s power2.in. Candidate C: strike-through draws scaleX 0→1 in 0.28s, then x 0→-220px out of frame. The panel's row counter tweens 5→6→5. The three asks pulse --brass 0.2s apart, then collapse into one card that scales 1.15→1 in 0.35s back.out(1.4) as its border draws.

lines.vo: The same failure three times becomes knowledge. Five times, it becomes a rule in your repo.
lines.scene: The ladder as motion, never as a diagram. Three shelves, one card climbing. A tally beside a MISTAKES.md entry increments `••` → `•••` and the card JUMPS one shelf up into `.tyran/knowledge/`. On the fifth dot it jumps again into a `CLAUDE.md` fence, with the `<!-- tyran:rules start -->` markers visible and the rule line carrying its signature and the five dated entries that earned it: `(worktree-missing-deps, 5 occurrences — MISTAKES.md entries 2026-05-02, 2026-06-11, 2026-07-03, 2026-07-28, 2026-08-09)`.
lines.animation: The third dot scales 0→1 in 0.2s back.out(2); on it the card tweens y -120px in 0.42s power3.out with a 6px overshoot and settle. Dots four and five land 0.35s apart. The second jump is another y -120px in 0.42s power3.out. The fence types its rule line at 34 chars/sec while the two comment markers hold at opacity 0.5. Three shelves, one card, and the two real thresholds.

lines.vo: That was one request. You made two calls. You still make every decision that matters.
lines.scene: Pull back to the desk, which has not left frame since shot three. It gains ONE new gold hairline segment — the lash advancing, and the specific thing this retro just added, so the callback motif is a mechanism rather than decoration. The board sits behind at 32% and is still alive. `.tyran/STOP` sits in hairline mono along the lower edge with its one line: `echo "wrong branch — hold everything" > .tyran/STOP`.
lines.animation: Camera scale 1.06→1.0 over 1.8s sine.inOut. The new lash segment draws stroke-dashoffset 180→0 in 0.6s power2.inOut. Behind, an age chip flips `2 h`→`2 h 1 m` and a second chip's colour tweens --brass→--sage over 0.4s. The STOP line fades 0→0.7 in 0.4s and holds.

lines.vo: Two commands inside Claude Code, then slash tyran setup. It's open source.
lines.scene: A LIVE end card, held at least four seconds. Two install lines in mono — `/plugin marketplace add jjanczur/tyran` and `/plugin install tyran@tyran` — with `/tyran:setup` beneath them and a caret blinking after it. The gold lash planted in frame one completes into the jackal lockup. A hairline row underneath: `Apache-2.0 · zero runtime dependencies · Claude Code ≥ 2.1`. The drawn lockup line: `The more you use it, the better it gets.` Behind it all at 20%, the board is still ticking. One destination, no star request, no email.
lines.animation: The three commands type in sequence at 24 chars/sec, 0.25s apart. The lash's final stroke draws stroke-dashoffset 260→0 in 0.9s power2.inOut and closes into the lockup, which scales 0.96→1 over 0.6s power2.out. The caret blinks on a 1.1s CSS loop. Behind, one board age counter increments once during the hold and one agent chip changes colour — the last moving thing on screen is the product, and nothing freezes.

design.visualSpine: THE DESK EMITS AND TAKES BACK. One element carries every scene: a brass-railed conductor card, centre-left, the only thing in the film that ever faces the viewer square-on (in board shots it persists as a 3px brass rail down the left edge of frame). Agents are ALWAYS off-axis, smaller, steel-railed, in uneven columns — that single asymmetry reads as hierarchy with no labels: the manager faces you, the team faces the work. lines.vo: This is the whole first session. Install it, set it up on a real repo, run something, read the board.
lines.scene: Cold open, no fade, on warm near-black #12100e. A 1px gold hairline enters from the left edge and stays — the conductor rail, planted at frame one. Centre-left it thickens and resolves into THE DESK: a brass-railed card, empty except a blinking caret, the only element in the film that ever faces the viewer square-on. At the right edge an eight-row chapter index types itself in mono at 40%: `01 install · 02 set up · 03 run it · 04 the board · 05 answer · 06 spend · 07 the gates · 08 the retro`. No board yet, no logo, no music sting.
lines.animation: Gold hairline scaleX 0→1 over 0.7s sine.out from a left transform-origin, then width 1px→3px in 0.3s. The desk's border draws itself via stroke-dashoffset 460→0 in 0.55s power2.inOut. The eight index rows fade opacity 0→0.4 with x -12px→0, 0.28s power2.out each, at unequal stagger 0.10 / 0.15 / 0.12 / 0.17 / 0.11 / 0.16 / 0.13 / 0.18 — never a uniform stagger. The caret blinks on a 1.1s CSS loop and keeps blinking through the gap.

lines.vo: One idea to hold on to. Tyran is a manager for a team of agents. You stay the stakeholder.
lines.scene: The desk holds `/tyran` typed in mono, still square-on. Four steel-railed agent cards rise behind it at 16% opacity, off-axis, smaller, in two uneven columns at four different heights — dark, unlit, facing the work rather than the viewer. No arrows, no org chart, no labels: the hierarchy is scale, axis and light. A single hairline note under the desk, drawn not spoken: `you describe it · Tyran plans it · agents do it`.
lines.animation: `/tyran` types at 14 chars/sec. The four agent cards tween opacity 0→0.16 and scale 0.9→1 in 0.35s power2.out at unequal stagger 0.13 / 0.19 / 0.16 / 0.22, landing at y offsets -40 / +18 / -12 / +52px. On the word "manager" the desk's rail colour tweens --brass #a8863c → --brass-bright #cfae63 over 0.25s and back. The hairline note fades 0→0.55 in 0.4s and holds through the chapter break.

lines.vo: Chapter one. Install is two slash commands inside Claude Code. Then restart. Hooks and agents load at session start.
lines.scene: Chapter card `01 · INSTALL` in gold hairline caps, top-left, with a rule under it; the desk stays in frame at 30% and the chapter index's first row goes brass. A terminal panel rises and types the real commands: `/plugin marketplace add jjanczur/tyran`, then `/plugin install tyran@tyran`. Beneath them, drawn and never spoken: `restart Claude Code — hooks and agents are read when a session starts`. No download bar, no browser chrome.
lines.animation: Chapter card y -20px→0, opacity 0→1, 0.3s power2.out; its rule draws scaleX 0→1 in 0.4s power2.inOut. Index row 01 tweens colour --muted #a29788 → --brass over 0.3s. Terminal panel y +90px→0, opacity 0→1, 0.45s power3.out. The two commands type at 24 chars/sec, 0.3s apart. On the word "restart" the panel border tweens --hairline #3b342c → --gold-dim #6d5410 and back over 0.5s, and the four dark agent cards behind blink to opacity 0 and back to 0.16 in 0.35s — the session restarting, drawn once and never explained.

lines.vo: Slash tyran hello is the smoke test. If it answers, you are running. The only requirement is Claude Code two point one.
lines.scene: `/tyran:hello` types into the same terminal and its answer prints as three mono lines: the resolved plugin root, then `4 agents`, then `14 skills`. A hairline row settles across the foot, drawn only: `Apache-2.0 · zero runtime dependencies · never writes into your ~/.claude`. The desk's ledger line gains its first sage `+1`.
lines.animation: Command types at 20 chars/sec. The three answer lines fade opacity 0→1 with x -8px→0 at stagger 0.11 / 0.16 / 0.13, 0.22s power2.out each; the `4` and the `14` tween from 0 with GSAP snap:1 over 0.4s. The ledger `+1` fades up in --sage #88a06a over 0.25s. The hairline row fades 0→0.55 in 0.4s. Index row 01 tweens --brass → --sage as the chapter closes, and that colour settle is the visual event inside the gap.

lines.vo: Chapter two. Slash tyran setup, once per repository. It reads how the repo is really worked. Not how a README describes it.
lines.scene: Chapter card `02 · SET UP`; index row 02 goes brass. `/tyran:setup` types on the desk. To its right a scan readout builds itself in two mono columns — the value on the left, the fact that produced it on the right: `package manager   npm            package-lock.json` / `validation        npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test      package.json scripts` / `languages         js 71% · md 22%` / `autonomy          P1             git log: last 50 merges are PRs, main is protected`. Nothing is asked yet; this is the pass that happens before any question.
lines.animation: Command types at 20 chars/sec. Each readout row's LEFT column types at 30 chars/sec, and its RIGHT evidence column fades opacity 0→0.75 exactly 0.18s later — so the fact visibly arrives behind the value rather than with it. Rows land at unequal stagger 0.14 / 0.21 / 0.16 / 0.24. Behind the readout a cyan #8fd8ea wash at opacity 0.2 sweeps top→bottom once over 0.8s linear via background-position — reading, not writing.

lines.vo: Every value it infers carries the fact that produced it. And it never grants itself the right to merge to main.
lines.scene: The readout collapses into the real file. `.tyran/config.yaml` draws, and the camera snaps onto the provenance block verbatim: `autonomy:` / `  value: P1` / `  source: 'git log: last 50 merges are PRs, main is protected'` / `  confidence: 0.9` / `  needs_confirmation: false`. A hairline tag beneath: `P1 branch-only · P2 staging · P3 merge to main — setup never infers P3`.
lines.animation: Snap-to 0.35s power3.inOut, scaling the block 1→1.3 while every other line in the file tweens to opacity 0.22 over the same 0.35s. The `source:` line types at 34 chars/sec. `0.9` counts up from 0 with one decimal over 0.4s. In the hairline tag, `P3` tweens colour --muted → --clay #c07a70 for 0.4s and back — refused, not offered — and that flicker is the only red in the chapter. The desk caret keeps blinking off-frame-left throughout.

lines.vo: Then commit the dot tyran folder. Agents work in git worktrees, and a worktree carries no untracked files.
lines.scene: Two commands type, exactly as setup asks for them: `git add .tyran` and `git commit -m "chore: adopt Tyran"`. Beside them four small worktree cards sit in an uneven row; while `.tyran` is uncommitted each carries a muted hairline tag `no policy · no config`. The commit lands and all four gain a brass edge as the tag flips to `policy · config`. Drawn beneath, for later: `/tyran:doctor — is any gate installed but unable to fire`.
lines.animation: Commands type at 22 chars/sec. The four worktree cards fade in at 0.14 stagger with tags in --muted. On the commit's ENTER a brass pulse travels left→right across them, each card's border tweening --hairline → --brass-edge #5d4c22 in 0.25s power2.out with x-keyframes 0.12s apart, and each tag cross-fading to its new text in 0.2s. A sage `+1` fades up on the desk ledger. Index row 02 settles --brass → --sage during the gap.

lines.vo: Chapter three. Type slash tyran and describe the work. He interviews you first. At most four questions.
lines.scene: Chapter card `03 · RUN IT`; index row 03 goes brass. Your words arrive from off-frame top in the SANS face, gold, unaligned to any grid, carrying a real drop shadow: `make the settings tab write, without losing my comments`. They land on the desk. Four question rows type in beneath, each with a muted `recommend:` line under it, and a corner counter reading `4 / 4`.
lines.animation: The sentence drops y -120px→0 with opacity 0→1 in 0.5s power3.out; on contact the desk rail flashes --brass-bright for 0.2s and returns. Question rows type at 22 chars/sec at unequal stagger 0.13 / 0.19 / 0.16 / 0.14; each `recommend:` line fades opacity 0→0.6 exactly 0.18s after its own question lands. The corner counter tweens 0→4 with GSAP snap:1 over 0.5s. The fourth caret keeps blinking.

lines.vo: After you accept the plan, the questions stop. Shall I continue is forbidden in the conductor's own file.
lines.scene: A fifth question row begins to draw, is struck through, and is replaced in place by the file's own sentence in mono: `"Shall I continue?" is forbidden.   skills/run/SKILL.md`. A hairline tag holds beneath the batch: `after the plan is accepted: zero questions except at gates`. Behind, the four dark agent cards begin to warm from 16% — the team is about to be sent.
lines.animation: The fifth row's strike-through draws scaleX 0→1 in 0.3s power2.inOut from a left origin; that row then fades opacity 1→0 over 0.25s while the file quote fades 0→1 across exactly the same 0.25s — a substitution, never a dissolve. The provenance chip `skills/run/SKILL.md` fades 0→0.6→0 across 1.0s. The four agent cards tween opacity 0.16→0.3 over 0.6s power1.inOut, which is the motion that carries the gap.

lines.vo: Then the team goes out. A scout reads the repo first. Cheap tier, read only, fresh context.
lines.scene: THE SPLAY. Agent cards are born at the desk's exact rect and travel to steel-railed columns, off-axis, at unequal distances and unequal arrival times. The scout leaves first, lands nearest, and is the smallest card; its three-line micro-terminal scrolls a fixed list: `git log --oneline -20`, `ls scripts/`, `command -v gitleaks`. To the right the real routing block types on under its own header comment verbatim — `# The ONLY place model names appear.` — with the model column masked to `····` so the header explains the restraint: `cheap ···· # scout, mechanical sweeps, ledger bookkeeping` / `work  ···· # DEFAULT: implementation and ordinary review` / `deep  ···· # root-cause diagnosis, hard implementation, risky review` / `top   ···· # security review, arbitration, final acceptance`. A cyan lamp lights over each tier as its line lands.
lines.animation: GSAP fromTo seeded from the desk's own getBoundingClientRect so the cards visibly come OUT of it: x/y from desk centre to column position, scale 0.35→1, 0.55s power2.out, arrivals 0.5s / 0.62s / 0.71s. The YAML header types at 20 chars/sec, then the four lines at 26 chars/sec, 0.18s apart; as each lands its lamp's cyan #8fd8ea opacity rises to its tier level — cheap 0.28, work 0.50, deep 0.70, top 0.90 — in 0.25s power2.out. The scout's micro-terminal steps y by -22px every 0.4s through its three fixed lines. No arrows, no radial fan, no connecting lines.

lines.vo: Implementers take one story each, on their own branch. Every one starts with an empty scrollback.
lines.scene: Two implementer cards land further out, each labelled with its own branch: `T-6/sandbox` and `T-7/spend-ledger`. The point is what is NOT in them — each scrollback panel is empty except a single handoff line, `ticket T-7 · files: scripts/cost.mjs, docs/cost.md`. Beside them a dense grey column of ~40 dim lines rises once for contrast, the one-chat scrollback, and is pushed out of frame for good. Then one mono path draws across the bottom and holds: `.tyran/state/<init>/journal.jsonl · committed to your repo`.
lines.animation: Two cards emitted from the desk rect with unequal travel (280px / 420px) and unequal arrival (0.5s / 0.68s, power2.out). The grey column translates y 0→-260px over 1.1s power1.in with opacity 1→0. The journal path types at 22 chars/sec. Simultaneously the scout chip collapses scale 1→0.4 and travels BACK along its exact outbound path in 0.6s power2.inOut to land on the desk, where a sage `+1` fades up on the ledger line — the first proof that a cheap agent finishes while the others are still out.

lines.vo: The reviewer has no editing tools at all. A reviewer who can fix what they found approves their own patch.
lines.scene: The reviewer card arrives last, on the far axis. Its real tool grant types in: `Read  Grep  Glob  Bash  WebFetch  WebSearch`. Then a second row draws — `Edit · Write · NotebookEdit` — and a rule is drawn straight through it. No red, no warning icon; the absence is the point. A one-second muted provenance chip fades under it: `agents/reviewer.md`. Two implementer terminals keep scrolling behind.
lines.animation: Card arrives 0.5s power2.out. Tools type at 26 chars/sec. The three editor names fade opacity 0→1, then a 1px rule draws scaleX 0→1 across them in 0.3s power2.inOut and they settle to opacity 0.3. The provenance chip fades 0→0.6→0 across 1.0s. Never fewer than two independent motions in flight: the struck row and the two scrolling terminals. Index row 03 settles --brass → --sage during the chapter break.

lines.vo: Chapter four. Open the board. One command, and this is the one place a Node version matters.
lines.scene: Chapter card `04 · THE BOARD`; index row 04 goes brass. A terminal types `npx @jjanczur/tyran board --dir .tyran --serve --write` and prints its real answer: `board: serving http://127.0.0.1:4173/`. Two hairline notes beneath, drawn: `--write turns on the Settings tab and the answer box` and `inside a session: /tyran:status regenerates it and tells you where it is`. Then the BOARD ARRIVES as one object — never a fade, never a scaled screenshot — rebuilt natively at the board's own tokens, header `Tyran board · 3 initiative(s) · 8/17 tickets merged (47%)`, above the real five-tab bar that stays on screen for every board shot from here on: `Overview · Board · Waiting on you (2) · Spend · Settings`. The five tab labels stagger in at 0.09 / 0.13 / 0.11 / 0.15 / 0.12, and `(2)` on Waiting on you lands last and holds a 0.3s --brass pulse, planting the promise this cut pays off at line 18.

lines.vo: Overview answers one question. Is anything on fire. Two waiting on you. Five agents running. Forty-seven percent merged.
lines.scene: The camera arrives on Overview; the board has been live since the previous line, so it is not re-introduced. Four tiles at their real values: WAITING ON YOU `2` / `answer them on the next tab` · AGENTS RUNNING `5` / `across 3 initiative(s)` · PROGRESS `47%` / `8 of 17 merged` · NEEDS A HUMAN `4` / `1 blocked · 1 changes requested · 2 agent(s) blocked`. Drawn above the strip, never spoken: `stalest first — sorted on what an agent SHOWED, not on what it said`.

lines.vo: The Board tab is every ticket, in exactly one of ten lanes. Moving a ticket means appending an event.
lines.scene: A lateral pan, no cut — the board stays one continuous object underneath and the tab bar never leaves. The real lanes in the real order with real titles: WAITING-OPERATOR (1) `T-4 — the Settings tab itself`, PAUSED-LIMIT (1) `T-3 — the resume watcher and its scheduled wake-up`, BLOCKED (1) `T-5 — a reboot-surviving resume`, CHANGES-REQUESTED (1), IN-REVIEW (1) `T-5 — the waiting-on-you queue and the answer sheet`, IN-PROGRESS (1) `T-6 — a clickable sandbox published with the docs`, READY (1) `T-7 — the spend ledger`, BACKLOG (1), PARKED (1), DONE (8). Mid-pan one card crosses IN-REVIEW → DONE by itself, and a muted receipt appears under the top hairline: `journal: merge T-5 · appended`, then fades on its own.

On contact: font-family swaps to mono, rotation 2.5°→0, text-align snaps left, all in 0.18s power4.out — mechanical, not magical — landing exactly on the word "ticket". The border draws stroke-dashoffset 640→0 clockwise in 0.45s power2.inOut. The card drops y -220px→0 with back.out(1.7) in 0.5s; the lane border warms --brass-edge for 0.3s; brightness 0.88→1 in 0.3s. The receipt fades 0→1 in 0.25s, holds 0.9s, fades out in 0.5s, which is what fills the gap.

lines.vo: Chapter five. The queue carries its open count in the tab label. A question you cannot see is a question you do not answer.
lines.scene: Chapter card `05 · ANSWER IT` drawn at 25% OVER the still-live board — never a full stop, the lanes keep ticking behind it. Then a snap-to onto `Waiting on you (2)`; the panel SLIDES under the same persistent tab bar rather than dissolving to a new page. Above the queue the three real commands print exactly as the tab prints them: `npx @jjanczur/tyran answer render --dir .tyran`, `$EDITOR .tyran/state/ANSWERS.md`, `npx @jjanczur/tyran answer apply --dir .tyran`, with the three answer words beside them: `blank takes the recorded default · a dash leaves it open · anything else is your answer`.
lines.animation: Chapter card fades 0→0.9 in 0.25s and back out over 0.4s while the board holds at 25% behind it, so momentum survives the break. Snap-to 0.35s power3.inOut. Panel x +80px→0 with opacity 0.3→1 in 0.4s. The three commands type at 34 chars/sec, 0.2s apart. The `(2)` in the tab label pulses --brass → --brass-bright once over 0.3s. Index row 05 goes brass.

lines.vo: Each card says whether a default is recorded. Type your answer. Press Answer. And the run carries on.
lines.scene: One real question card, rebuilt natively at legible weight, revealed in the order that IS the argument: the kind tag `DECISION · A DEFAULT IS RECORDED`, then the question verbatim — `The board reloads itself every 30 seconds, which wipes a half-typed model name. Pause the refresh while the Settings tab is open, or keep the page always-live and accept the loss?` — then `RECOMMENDATION  pause it while Settings is open — the other three tabs stay live, and an unsaved field is the only thing at risk`, then `DEFAULT`, then `BLOCKS 1 ticket(s): T-5`. A caret types a short answer, the Answer button flashes brass, the card collapses to one sage line, and the tab label ticks (2) → (1). Hairline note: `needs the board started with --write`. No cursor graphic anywhere; the state change is the interaction.
lines.animation: Card rows reveal top-down, y 8px→0 with opacity 0→1, 0.25s power2.out each, stagger 0.14. The answer types at 18 chars/sec. The button background tweens --brass-low #221c11 → --brass #a8863c and back over 0.2s. The card height tweens to a single line in 0.35s power2.inOut as its rail turns --sage. The tab count swaps 2→1 LAST, and that decrement is the final thing the eye catches before the panel slides away.

lines.vo: Spend is what it cost. By model, by agent type, by ticket. The scout's whole reconnaissance was three cents.
lines.scene: Chapter tag `06 · SPEND` drawn small; index row 06 goes brass. The Spend panel slides in under the same tab bar — a native rebuild at board tokens, never a scaled capture. Tiles: `TOKENS 4.5 M / 404 requests`, `COST THROUGH THE API $16.97`, `CONDUCTOR OVERHEAD 55% / of tokens, no ticket`, `ATTRIBUTED 5 / 6`. Then the by-agent-type rows draw in descending order at their real values, labelled by ROLE only: conductor $8.73, implementer $6.72, reviewer $1.48, and scout $0.03 — a sliver three pixels wide. The camera holds on the scout row while every other bar stays drawn; the arithmetic is left to the viewer and no savings figure is spoken or drawn. The by-model chart is deliberately not rendered in this cut, so no model name reaches a frame.
lines.animation: Panel x +80px→0 with opacity 0.3→1 in 0.4s. TOKENS tweens 0→4.5 with one decimal, `404` snaps with snap:1, `$16.97` counts up over 0.8s. Bars scaleX 0→1 from a left origin at unequal stagger 0.22 / 0.16 / 0.28, 0.45s each power2.out. The camera then holds 1.6s on the scout row while its label tweens --muted → --brass over 0.3s and its three-pixel bar sits finished beside three long ones.

lines.vo: Fifty-five percent of those tokens were the manager's own context. Its own row, so nothing hides. Tyran does not know what you pay. You write the rate card.
lines.scene: The CONDUCTOR OVERHEAD tile pulses once and holds at 55%. A hairline connector draws from the tile down to the conductor row, carrying the board's own sentence verbatim: `conductor context is not attributable to any ticket; it is its own row so the rows sum to the total`. Then the TOKENS | COST toggle visibly flips and every label re-renders from a dollar figure to a token count — a toggle that works on camera is proof of a live page. Drawn beneath, never spoken: the `pricing:` block with its four required rate keys, and the repo's own line `tokens are facts, money is an opinion`.
lines.animation: Tile border tweens --hairline #332e27 → --brass and back over 0.5s. A 1px connector draws scaleX 0→1 in 0.3s power2.inOut, then the sentence fades 0→0.85 over 0.3s and holds. The toggle's active pill slides x 0→-64px in 0.25s power3.inOut and every numeric label cross-fades to its token value over 0.3s. The doctrine line fades 0→0.8 in 0.4s. Index row 06 settles --brass → --sage during the chapter break.

lines.vo: Chapter seven. Two hooks will refuse things. A report with no command output is one. It blocks silence, not forgery.
lines.scene: Chapter tag `07 · THE GATES`; index row 07 goes brass. A terminal panel rises over the board, which keeps ticking behind it at 30%. A real-shaped report prints: `tyran:implementer — final report` / `Ran the suite — everything is green. Typecheck is clean. Ready to merge.` The caret hits the desk's brass rail and the block recoils once. The refusal's first line prints verbatim: `REFUSED by the tyran evidence gate: this report carries no raw command output.` Then the beat ENDS ON THE PASS — the report comes back carrying `# pass 343  # fail 0` and goes through, `EXIT=0` in sage. Drawn under the passed report: `it blocks silence, not forgery`. Behind, on the board, the `Errors logged (2)` row lights brass for a beat: the refusal has somewhere to be logged, and this is it.
lines.animation: Panel rises y +120px→0 with opacity 0→1 in 0.45s power3.out. The desk rail thickens 3px→6px across the caret's path over 0.3s — the stop is built before it is needed. The report block tweens x 0→-6px→0 in 0.12s power4.out, ONCE: no shake loop, no error triangle. The refusal line types at 40 chars/sec. The report cross-fades to its evidence-bearing version in 0.25s and its rail tweens --clay #c07a70 → --sage #88a06a over 0.3s. Behind, the board's `Errors logged (2)` row tweens border-colour --hairline → --brass and back over 0.6s. The concession line holds at opacity 0.7 through the gap.

lines.vo: And a commit carrying a secret is refused. Even inside a markdown file. Install gitleaks first, or that gate has nothing to scan with.
lines.scene: Show what is in danger FIRST: a diff of three ordinary files, and a fourth line carrying `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA••••••••••••`, elided on screen exactly as the gate elides it — a refusal must never republish the secret. Then `git commit -m "wire up the uploader"` types itself. It is an ordinary, well-intentioned command, and that is the point. It recoils against the same brass rail. One `REFUSED` tag in clay for well under a second; the refusal body in muted text ending `(4812 bytes, coverage verified)`. Then the pass: the line becomes `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=${env}`, the command re-runs, and `EXIT=0` prints in sage. Drawn beneath: `brew install gitleaks`, and the gate's own stated limit — `not a guarantee — a mechanical check at the point the damage becomes permanent`.
lines.animation: Diff lines fade in at 0.09 stagger; the key line's background lifts to --gold-low #2a2110 for 0.4s then settles back. The command types at 18 chars/sec. The identical 0.12s power4.out recoil, played once at 1.2× the previous beat's speed, so the rhythm itself becomes legible as "this is what a gate does". The REFUSED tag fades 0→1 in 0.1s, holds 0.6s, out in 0.2s. The refusal body types at 30 chars/sec. The key line cross-fades to `${env}` in 0.15s, the command re-types at 24 chars/sec, and `EXIT=0` fades up in --green #8fce6a over 0.25s. The frame's accent settles from clay back to brass across 0.4s — red is the verdict, gold is what the shot is left holding.

lines.vo: Chapter eight. When the last ticket merges, try to end the session. It refuses. Once.
lines.scene: Chapter tag `08 · THE RETRO`; index row 08 goes brass. Back to the desk — the spine closing. Every ticket of the initiative comes home as sage-railed cards and compresses into one line: `initiative closed · 7 tickets · 4 agents`. The closing line types, and the Stop hook refuses it exactly once, in muted text: `tyran: initiative "the-board" has all 7 of its tickets merged and no retrospective recorded since the last merge.` A hairline note beneath, drawn: `deciding NOT to run one is a legitimate answer — record it and it never asks again`.
lines.animation: The done cards travel back along their own outbound paths in 0.7s power2.inOut and collapse into a single line via a height tween in 0.3s power2.inOut, the ledger incrementing in sage as each lands. The refusal types at 42 chars/sec; the phrase `no retrospective recorded` tweens colour --muted → --clay over 0.35s and holds — one clay phrase, under a second of full saturation, and no icon. The hairline note fades 0→0.6 in 0.4s.

lines.vo: It reads the journals and the reports, then changes Tyran itself. Never your product code. Most retros change nothing, and that is correct.
lines.scene: The retro agent spawns LAST, after everything else has already come home, and it READS rather than writes: a cyan scan-line sweeps a tall thin column of mono journal lines. Then three fates resolve at three different moments in ONE frame, because a promotion without a visible rejection reads as bloat. (a) A candidate rises and HARDENS into the knowledge panel — sans becoming mono — gaining the id `K-12` and an `applies_to` glob. (b) A second meets four small gates, `recurs? · cost measured? · already covered? · one sentence?`, fails on the third, and drops out of frame. (c) An existing rule carrying `helped 0 / 6` is struck through and slides out. The panel ends holding the same number of rows it started with.
lines.animation: A CSS linear-gradient band 120px tall sweeps the journal column y -100%→+100% over 1.2s linear — light moving over text, nothing written yet. Candidate A: y +30px→0 with a font-family swap and a border drawing stroke-dashoffset 480→0 in 0.4s power2.inOut. Candidate B: its four gates light 0.18s apart, the third flashing --clay for 0.35s, then B tweens filter grayscale 0→1 with y 0→+140px and opacity→0 over 0.5s power2.in. Candidate C: strike-through draws scaleX 0→1 in 0.28s, then x 0→-220px out of frame. The panel's row counter tweens 5→6→5, and that arithmetic on screen is the whole anti-bloat claim.

lines.vo: The same failure three times becomes knowledge, pasted into every matching handoff. Five times, it becomes a rule in your CLAUDE file.
lines.scene: The ladder as motion, never as a diagram. Three shelves, one card climbing. A tally beside a `MISTAKES.md` entry increments `••` → `•••` and the card JUMPS one shelf up into `.tyran/knowledge/`. On the fifth dot it jumps again into a `CLAUDE.md` fence, with the `<!-- tyran:rules start -->` markers visible and the rule line carrying its signature and the dated entries that earned it: `(worktree-missing-deps, 5 occurrences — MISTAKES.md entries 2026-05-02, 2026-06-11, 2026-07-03, 2026-07-28, 2026-08-09)`. A hairline note: `you say no by deleting the line`. The desk's gold outline gains ONE new hairline segment — the lash advancing, and the specific thing this retro just added.
lines.animation: The third dot scales 0→1 in 0.2s back.out(2); on it the card tweens y -120px in 0.42s power3.out with a 6px overshoot and settle. Dots four and five land 0.35s apart. The second jump is another y -120px in 0.42s power3.out. The fence types its rule line at 34 chars/sec while the two comment markers hold at opacity 0.5. The new lash segment draws stroke-dashoffset 180→0 in 0.6s power2.inOut. Index row 08 settles --brass → --sage, and all eight rows are now sage.

lines.vo: One line in a STOP file halts everything, from anywhere. You keep every decision. The team does the rest.
lines.scene: A LIVE end card, held at least four seconds. `echo "wrong branch — hold everything" > .tyran/STOP` types in mono along the lower edge, and the board behind it — still alive at 30% — grows a clay `STOPPED` banner above its tiles carrying the file's first line as its reason. Then the two install lines sit centre with `/tyran:setup` beneath them and a caret blinking after it. The gold lash planted in frame one completes into the jackal lockup. A hairline row underneath: `Apache-2.0 · zero runtime dependencies · Claude Code ≥ 2.1`. The drawn lockup line: `The more you use it, the better it gets.` One destination, no star request, no email, no waitlist.
lines.animation: The STOP line types at 22 chars/sec; on ENTER the board's STOPPED banner draws its border stroke-dashoffset 520→0 in 0.4s power2.out and its text fades 0→0.9 in --clay. The three commands type in sequence at 24 chars/sec, 0.25s apart. The lash's final stroke draws stroke-dashoffset 260→0 in 0.9s power2.inOut and closes into the lockup, which scales 0.96→1 over 0.6s power2.out. The caret blinks on a 1.1s CSS loop. Behind, during the hold, one board age counter increments once and one agent chip's colour tweens --brass → --sage over 0.4s — the last moving thing on screen is the product, and nothing freezes.

slate.title: The Mistake
slate.purpose: Make a senior developer recognise their own last session in the first second — one expensive model doing every job in one swelling context — and land a single fix they can check: a manager who routes each piece to its own agent at its own tier, each starting clean, with the real bill as the proof.

lines.vo: Your most expensive model just renamed a variable.
lines.scene: Cold open, no fade, no title card. One terminal panel 900px wide sits high in frame (y 300-740) on warm near-black #12100e, lit by a single cyan wash pooling from above — cyan is a light source here and stays one for the whole cut. Mono at 34px types `rename userSvc -> userService`, then prints `3 files changed`. A gold-on-stone chip on the panel's top right reads TOP TIER at 28px mono. Behind the panel, a clipped column of about 40 dim grey scrollback lines is ALREADY scrolling before the first word is spoken. A 1px gold hairline enters at the left edge of frame and stays: the conductor rail, planted at frame one.
lines.animation: #panel-one is fully composed at frame 0 — tl.set('#panel-one',{autoAlpha:1}) at t=0, nothing fades in, the shot is already running when the viewer arrives. #cmd-1 reveals by clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0 0% 0 0) at 18 chars/sec, ease 'none'; #out-1 then autoAlpha 0->1 in 0.18s. #chip-top scale 1.18->1, back.out(2.2), 0.28s at t=0.35 — the price tag is legible before the sentence finishes. #wash-cold opacity pinned at 0.55 and never touched again in this beat: the meter is on, and it does not dim. #scroll-grey translateY 0->-180px over 2.6s ease 'none' inside its own overflow:hidden box, so its top line is physically pushed out. #rail scaleY 0->1, transform-origin top, 0.8s sine.out.

lines.vo: Then in the same chat, it judged an auth boundary.
lines.scene: No cut, same panel. A second command types beneath the first — `review the auth boundary in api/session.ts` — and an identical TOP TIER chip appears beside it. Between the two rows a 1px hairline connector and one muted mono tag: `same context · same rate`. The grey scrollback behind grows taller and keeps climbing out of its own box. Nothing is red; this is a diagnosis, not an accusation.
lines.animation: #cmd-2 clip-path reveal at 20 chars/sec, ease 'none'. #chip-top-2 autoAlpha 0->1 in 0.2s, then both chips tween border-color --gold-dim -> --gold and back over 0.35s, offset 0.12s from each other — never a uniform stagger. #tag-same autoAlpha 0->0.85, y 6->0, 0.25s power2.out. #scroll-grey height 46%->82% over 1.4s power1.in while its translateY continues unbroken — so the 0.45s gap that follows still has two things moving in it.

lines.vo: One chat. One model. Every single job.
lines.scene: The camera pulls back and the panel is suddenly small and alone in a large dark frame. Three mono stamps land down the right side at 34px: ONE CHAT / ONE MODEL / EVERY JOB. Above the panel a single cyan lamp burns at full. No dollar figure, no token counter — the image is the claim, and the claim is that one light has been on the whole time.
lines.animation: #stage-one scale 1.0->0.86 and y 0->+50px over 1.8s sine.inOut — the camera acts, the layout holds. .stamp y 12->0, autoAlpha 0->1, 0.22s power2.out at unequal stagger 0.11 / 0.17 / 0.24. #lamp-one opacity fixed at 0.95 and deliberately never animated — it is the one light in this cut that never changes, and that is the point. #scroll-grey keeps climbing underneath throughout.

lines.vo: That is why the bill is high, and the work gets worse.
lines.scene: The grey scrollback fills the panel from the bottom until only two live lines are left at the top, and those two dim as the stack swallows them. One mono line under the panel: `one context · re-read every turn`, caret blinking after it. The lamp stays at full. The frame reads as a room with one lamp left on all night.
lines.animation: #scroll-grey height 82%->94% over 1.5s power1.in; .live-line opacity 1->0.45 over 0.6s as the stack rises behind them. #tag-context autoAlpha 0->0.8 in 0.3s power2.out, its caret blinking on a 1.1s CSS steps loop that carries straight through the 0.55s gap. #lamp-one holds 0.95, unmoved. No red wash anywhere in this cut — red is reserved for a refusal, and this beat refuses nothing.

lines.vo: No good team puts a principal engineer on a grep.
lines.scene: Three job rows stack in the middle of frame, each currently carrying the SAME gold TOP TIER chip: `grep the changelog` · `rename the handler` · `judge the auth boundary`. On the line, the top two chips desaturate and slide off their rows and out of frame, and only the chip on `judge the auth boundary` stays gold and gains a soft gold bloom. The argument is drawn rather than narrated: exactly one of these three needs the expensive tier. The gold rail on the left edge thickens as it happens.
lines.animation: .job rows y 14->0, autoAlpha 0->1, 0.26s power2.out at unequal stagger 0.13 / 0.19. #chip-a and #chip-b tween filter grayscale(0)->grayscale(1), x 0->-40px, autoAlpha 1->0 over 0.4s power2.in, 0.15s apart. #chip-c border-color -> --gold and box-shadow none -> 0 0 28px rgba(212,160,23,.28) over 0.35s power2.out. #rail width 1px->3px in 0.3s sine.out.

lines.vo: Tyran is the manager. You brief him once.
lines.scene: THE DESK. The gold rail resolves into a brass-railed card, centre-left — the only element in this cut that ever faces the viewer square-on. The one-chat panel shrinks off-axis to the right, dims, and keeps one grey line scrolling as a reminder that it is still burning. Your words arrive from off-frame top in the SANS face, gold, unaligned to any grid, carrying a real drop shadow: `ship the settings tab without losing my comments`. They land on the desk, and `/tyran` sits drawn in mono beneath — the command is never spoken. Four steel-railed agent cards fade up behind at 14%, dark and unlit, in two uneven columns: off-axis, smaller, facing the work rather than the viewer.
lines.animation: #desk border draws itself on an inline SVG rect, stroke-dashoffset 420->0 in 0.5s power2.inOut. #stage-one scale ->0.4, x +300px, autoAlpha 1->0.3 over 0.7s power3.inOut. #brief drops y -140->0 with autoAlpha 0->1 in 0.5s power3.out; on contact #desk-rail background-color --brass -> --brass-bright for 0.2s and back. .agent autoAlpha 0->0.14 at unequal stagger 0.13 / 0.19 / 0.16 / 0.22 — never a symmetrical fan, never a connecting arrow.

lines.vo: A scout reads the repo first. Cheap tier, read only.
lines.scene: THE SPLAY. The scout card is born at the desk's own rectangle and travels out to a steel-railed column, off-axis — it leaves first, lands nearest, and is the smallest card in frame. Its three-line micro-terminal scrolls a fixed, deterministic list: `git log --oneline -20`, `ls scripts/`, `command -v gitleaks`. A cyan lamp above the scout column comes up DIM and stays dim. A hairline under the card: `read-only · cheap tier`.
lines.animation: gsap.fromTo seeded from #desk.getBoundingClientRect() so the card visibly comes OUT of the desk: x/y from desk centre to column position, scale 0.35->1, autoAlpha 0->1, 0.55s power2.out. #lamp-scout opacity 0->0.28 in 0.3s and HOLDS there — dim, and on almost continuously. The micro-terminal steps translateY by -34px every 0.4s through its three fixed lines, 0.12s power2.out per step, and keeps stepping through the gap. No radial fan, no org-chart boxes, no arrows.

lines.vo: Implementers take one story each, on their own branch.
lines.scene: Two implementer cards land further out at unequal distances, each labelled with its own branch: `T-6/sandbox` and `T-7/spend-ledger`. What matters is what is NOT in them — each scrollback panel is empty except a single handoff line, `ticket T-7 · files: scripts/cost.mjs, docs/cost.md`. At the same time the scout collapses to a chip and travels home along the exact path it left on, and a sage `+1` appears on the desk's ledger line. Cheap agents finish and come back while the others are still out.
lines.animation: Two .impl cards emitted from the desk rect, travelling 300px and 430px and arriving in 0.5s and 0.68s (power2.out) — unequal distance, unequal arrival. Their handoff line reveals by clip-path at 26 chars/sec. Simultaneously #chip-scout scale 1->0.4 and tweens back along its outbound x/y coordinates in 0.6s power2.inOut, landing on #desk, where #ledger-plus autoAlpha 0->1 and y 6->0 in 0.25s in --sage. Minimum two independent motions in flight for the whole beat.

lines.vo: None of them re-reads your conversation. None inherits six failed attempts.
lines.scene: A hard side-by-side, held. Left: the old one-chat column, a dense grey stack that keeps growing and pushes its one useful gold line out of the top of its own box. Right: an implementer panel with one line and a great deal of empty. Mono labels beneath each, 30px: `carries everything` / `carries the ticket`. Behind the right panel, six dim ghost lines reading `attempt 1` through `attempt 6` grey out and drop away — the failures a clean agent cannot inherit.
lines.animation: #scroll-grey translateY 0->-120px over 1.2s ease 'none', its gold line exiting the clip entirely. .ghost-attempt (six lines) tween filter grayscale(0)->grayscale(1), y 0->+90px, autoAlpha 1->0 over 0.45s power2.in at unequal stagger 0.07 / 0.11 / 0.09 / 0.13 / 0.08 / 0.12. The two labels autoAlpha 0->0.85 at 0.16 stagger. The right panel's caret blinks on a 1.1s CSS loop straight through the 0.5s gap.

lines.vo: Security review still gets the strongest tier. No setting can lower it.
lines.scene: The real routing block types on over the columns, under its own header comment verbatim: `# The ONLY place model names appear.` Four lines follow with their true inline comments and the model column MASKED to `····`, so the restraint is the subject rather than something hidden: `cheap ···· # scout, mechanical sweeps, ledger bookkeeping` / `work  ···· # DEFAULT: implementation and ordinary review` / `deep  ···· # root-cause diagnosis, hard implementation` / `top   ···· # security review, arbitration, final acceptance`. Each line lights one lamp on the right. Then a cheap override is thrown at security review, the top lamp dips and SNAPS back, and a mono tag prints: `floored: top`. Hairline beneath: `the floor is applied last, so it cannot be shifted out of`.
lines.animation: Header comment reveals at 20 chars/sec; the four tier lines at 26 chars/sec, 0.18s apart. As each lands, its lamp's cyan opacity rises to its tier level — cheap 0.28, work 0.50, deep 0.70, top 0.90 — in 0.25s power2.out. On the override: #lamp-top opacity 0.90->0.72 over 0.18s, then SNAPS to 0.90 in 0.12s power4.out — the escalation the product refuses to allow — and #tag-floor autoAlpha 0->1 in 0.2s. Through the following gap, #lamp-cheap pulses 0.28<->0.20 on a 0.6s sine yoyo while #lamp-top holds steady.

lines.vo: The scout's whole reconnaissance cost three cents. That is the bill, not an estimate.
lines.scene: The board's own Spend panel, rebuilt natively in HTML at the board's tokens (bg #1c1a16, hairline #332e27, --brass #a8863c, --brass-low #221c11, --steel #7d9ea9, --sage #88a06a) at phone-legible weight — never a scaled capture. The real five-tab strip sits above it at low emphasis with Spend in its brass pill, and gets no tour. BY AGENT TYPE draws in descending order, labelled by ROLE only: conductor $8.73 in the muted not-a-ticket tone, implementer $6.72, reviewer $1.48, then scout $0.03 as a sliver three pixels wide. Held in frame with the dollars so they are never naked: `4.5 M tokens · 404 requests`. Two hairline notes, drawn and never spoken: `conductor context is its own row, so the rows sum to the total` and `Tyran does not know what you pay. You write the rate card.`
lines.animation: #spend rises y +90->0 with autoAlpha 0.2->1 in 0.5s power3.out — the panel ARRIVES; the camera does not dissolve to it. .bar scaleX 0->1 from transform-origin left, 0.45s each power2.out, at unequal stagger 0.22 / 0.16 / 0.28. The `4.5 M` figure tweens 0->4.5 with one decimal and `404` snaps with snap:1 over 0.7s. The camera then holds 1.6s on the scout row while #row-scout's label colour tweens --muted -> --brass over 0.3s and every other bar stays fully drawn — the arithmetic is left to the viewer, and no savings figure is drawn or spoken anywhere.

lines.vo: One chat and one model. Or a team.
lines.scene: The last split, one second per side. Left: the opening frame returns — single lamp at full, grey stack filling the panel, one line of useful work left. Right: the desk with four lamps at their true levels, three of them dim and one dark. The total light in the right half is visibly lower. Two mono labels type across the bottom, drawn and never spoken: `one chat · one context · every job` under the left, `four tiers · fresh context each` under the right.
lines.animation: The two halves resolve into a 50/50 split by tweening clip-path inset(0 50% 0 0) on #half-left and inset(0 0 0 50%) on #half-right over 0.4s power2.inOut. #lamp-one holds 0.95 for the entire beat while the four .lamp elements run their true cycle: cheap steady at 0.28, work pulsing 0.50<->0.30 on a 0.6s sine yoyo, deep flaring to 0.70 once for 0.5s, top dark throughout. The two labels reveal by clip-path at 24 chars/sec, starting 0.12s apart.

lines.vo: Tyran. Open source. The board is live in your browser, nothing to install.
lines.scene: A LIVE end card, held for more than four seconds. The gold hairline planted at frame one completes into the jackal lockup, with the wordmark TYRAN at 90px beneath it. ONE destination, in mono at 34px: `jjanczur.github.io/tyran/sandbox`, and a hairline under it — `the real page, sample data, nothing to install`. Below that: `a Claude Code plugin · Apache-2.0 · zero runtime dependencies`. The drawn brand line: `The more you use it, the better it gets.` Behind everything at 18%, the native Spend panel is still there and still moving. No star request, no email address, no second destination.
