design.visualSpine: ONE LAMP, THEN FOUR — the same gesture as the locked explainer, compressed to a single argument. A 1px gold hairline is planted at the left edge in frame one and never leaves; at the turn it thickens and resolves into THE DESK, a brass-railed card centre-left that is the only element in the cut ever facing the viewer square-on. Agents are always off-axis, smaller, steel-railed, in uneven columns — the manager faces you, the team faces the work, and that asymmetry carries the hierarchy with no labels or diagrams. Every agent card is born at the desk's own getBoundingClientRect and travels an unequal distance to an unequal arrival; the scout leaves first, lands nearest, and folds back home along the exact path it left on while the implementers are still out. Against it, the one-chat panel from the cold open never dies — it shrinks off-axis, dims, and keeps one grey line scrolling to the last split, because the film's real subject is two lighting states of the same room.
motifs: LIGHT IS THE BILL — cyan #8fd8ea encodes cost and nothing else: glow intensity is tier strength, on-time is usage. The one-chat lamp is pinned at 0.95 from frame one and is deliberately the only light in the cut that never animates; the four tier lamps run cheap 0.28 near-continuous, work pulsing 0.50, deep flaring 0.70 once, top dark. The total light in the frame is the invoice. Cyan is never an accent, never a button, never a border.

WORDS HARDEN INTO OBJECTS — human input is sans, gold, unaligned, shadowed; machine state is mono, grid-aligned, bordered, flat. The brief lands on the desk in sans and the tier block, the handoff line and the spend rows answer in mono. Every transition between the two faces is a drawn border plus a face swap landing on a beat, never a crossfade.

THE SCROLLBACK THAT EATS THE FRAME — a clipped grey column, already scrolling before the first word, that grows from 46% to 94% of its panel and physically pushes its one useful gold line out of its own box. It is the whole 'why the work gets worse' argument, running under four separate lines without a word spent on it, and it is answered by an implementer panel that is almost entirely empty.

NOTHING FULLY STOPS — every declared voiceover gap carries a visual event: a scrollback still climbing, a caret blinking, a lamp pulsing on a sine yoyo, a micro-terminal stepping its next fixed line, an age flipping 2 min to 3 min. A gap is a place for motion, not for silence — which is the structural fix for 'the pauses are too long', not a TTS setting.

THE GOLD LASH, GIVEN A MECHANISM — one hairline planted at the left edge in frame one as the conductor rail, thickening into the desk at the turn, warming to --brass-bright the instant your words land on it, and finally closing into the jackal lockup. The landing frame is a loop closing, not a logo appearing.

EVERY NUMBER KEEPS ITS RECEIPT — $8.73 · $6.72 · $1.48 · $0.03 · 4.5 M tokens · 404 requests, all from video/assets/capture/hi-spend-cost.png, set in the board's own mono at the board's own tokens. Rows labelled by role, never by model; the token count is always in frame with the dollars; the rate-card concession is drawn verbatim; and no savings figure, percentage or multiple appears anywhere, because nothing in this repo measures one.
design.palette: Dark only, no exceptions. Ground is warm near-black --stone #12100e with --raised #1c1917 panels and #3b342c hairlines. Gold #d4a017 is the ONE accent and belongs to the operator and the conductor rail: the TOP TIER chips, the desk edge, the brief that arrives in sans, the lockup. Cyan #8fd8ea is a light source and this cut's cost meter — washes and lamps only, never a button, link, border or highlight. Sage #88a06a appears exactly once, as the desk's ledger `+1` when the scout comes home. RED APPEARS NOWHERE IN THIS CUT: there is no refusal beat here, and red only ever means refusal. The native Spend panel switches to the board's own tokens unchanged so drawn pixels and captured pixels are the same object — bg #1c1a16, hairline #332e27, --brass #a8863c, --brass-low #221c11 for the conductor's not-a-ticket row, --steel #7d9ea9, --sage #88a06a. System font stacks only, no web fonts, no gradients beyond the two radial washes, no bokeh, no light theme, no browser chrome.

slate.title: The Board — your agents move their own tickets
slate.purpose: The board-first short. It opens ON a live kanban that is already moving and never leaves it: ten lanes, a blocker that says how long it has stood still, a spoken aside that hardens into ticket T-9 with a journal receipt, a card an agent crosses into DONE by itself, a real question answered on the page with the tab count ticking 2 to 1, and the bill broken out by role until the scout's three cents does the arguing. It ends on the sandbox — click it yourself, nothing to install — because the board is the only proof the delegation story needs and the sandbox is that board, already published.

design.visualSpine: ONE BOARD, ONE OBJECT, NEVER RE-INTRODUCED. The board is on screen at frame zero, already in motion, and it is still on screen behind the end card. It is never cut to, never faded in, never dissolved between tabs: the camera moves (a lateral pan across the lane strip, a 0.35s snap-to onto a card) and panels slide horizontally UNDER a five-tab bar that is pinned for the entire film. Down the left edge of frame, from frame one, a 3px brass rail — the conductor's desk, the only element that never moves — so every shot is read as one page seen from different distances rather than a slideshow of screenshots. The whole board is rebuilt natively in HTML at the board's own tokens: a 2240px capture scaled into 1080 is unreadable on the device this will be watched on, and a native rebuild is the only way a ticket can actually cross a lane. Mono type never below 26px; load-bearing values 30-34px.
motifs: WORDS HARDEN INTO OBJECTS — your aside enters in the SANS face, gold, tilted 2.5 degrees off-grid, with a real drop shadow, floating over the lanes so it visibly does not belong there. A gold segment runs the top hairline and strikes it: the letterforms snap to MONO, snap left onto the lane grid, and a border DRAWS itself around them clockwise via stroke-dashoffset. A face swap plus a drawn border landing on a beat — never a crossfade.

EVERY LANE MOVE IS AN APPEND — each state change is followed half a second later by one muted mono receipt under the top hairline that fades on its own: `journal: report T-6 · appended`, `journal: ticket.declare T-9 · appended`. That line is the difference between a kanban demo and the claim that nothing you said can be lost.

NOTHING FULLY STOPS — in every frame at least one true-to-product number is moving, by preference an age counter, because the board genuinely computes ages in the reader's own browser. Every declared gap carries a visual event: a lane count incrementing, a rail warming, a bar finishing its draw, a receipt fading. The final frame has the board ticking behind the lockup.

NO CURSOR, NO CHROME — interaction is shown only as state change: aria-pressed brass fill on a selected card, a caret, a button flashing brass, a tab count decrementing. No pointer graphic, no browser frame, no drop-shadow card clichés on board surfaces.

RATIONED COLOUR — brass is the operator's own queue and the one accent; steel lights agents; clay is the only alarm on the page and appears exactly twice, each under a second, never as a fill; sage is the ledger plus. Cyan never appears as an accent here at all.

EVERY NUMBER KEEPS ITS RECEIPT — 3 initiatives · 8/17 (47%) → 9/17 (53%) · (2) → (1) · 4.5 M · 404 · $16.97 · 55% · 5/6 · $8.73 / $6.72 / $1.48 / $0.03 · 2.5 M / 1.6 M / 333.4 k / 108.2 k · no event 4 h · 3 HOURS since last signal. Every one exists in this repo or in the captures. No invented figure, nothing rounded for looks, and no savings percentage anywhere, because nothing in this repo measures one.
design.palette: Dark only, warm near-black, the board's own tokens so drawn pixels and captured pixels are the same object: bg #141210, raised #1c1a16, sunken #100e0c, hairline #332e27. --brass #a8863c / --brass-bright #cfae63 / --brass-low #221c11 / --brass-edge #5d4c22 is the single accent and marks the operator's queue. --steel #7d9ea9 lights agents. --clay #c07a70 is refusal and staleness, rationed to two sub-second appearances. --sage #88a06a is the ledger plus (done, EXIT=0). Text --bheading #ece5d7, --btext #cec7ba, --bmuted #8f8779; the incoming human sentence alone in --gold-bright #e8bc4d. System fonts only: ui-serif for the board's headings, ui-monospace for all machine state, ui-sans-serif for human input and burned captions. No purple-blue gradients, no bokeh, no light theme, no third accent.

lines.vo: Your agents have a Kanban board now.
lines.scene: Cold open, no fade, no logo — the board is ALREADY there and already moving. Native rebuild at the board's own tokens on warm near-black #141210. Top: `Tyran board` in the board's serif, and under it in mono `3 initiative(s) · 8/17 tickets merged (47%)`. Directly beneath, the real five-tab bar that stays pinned for the whole film: `Overview · Board · Waiting on you (2) · Spend · Settings`, with `Board` carrying the brass aria-pressed pill and the `(2)` planted in the queue label from the very first frame. Below that, three of the ten lanes fill the frame at phone scale — IN-PROGRESS (1) holding `T-6 — a clickable sandbox published with the docs  the-board`, READY (1) holding `T-7 — the spend ledger: what the work cost, by model and by ticket`, DONE (8) holding `T-4 — the localhost viewer, re-rendered per request`. A 3px brass rail runs down the left edge of frame. Card titles at 30px mono, lane headers at 24px uppercase.

lines.vo: And they move the tickets themselves.

There is no cursor anywhere on screen; the state change IS the interaction. IN-PROGRESS ticks (1) → (0), IN-REVIEW ticks (1) → (2). Half a second later one muted mono line appears under the top hairline and fades on its own: `journal: report T-6 · appended`.

The camera travels right across all ten lane headers in the board's own order, strongest verdict first: `WAITING-OPERATOR (1) · PAUSED-LIMIT (1) · BLOCKED (1) · CHANGES-REQUESTED (1) · IN-REVIEW (2) · IN-PROGRESS (0) · READY (1) · BACKLOG (1) · PARKED (1) · DONE (8)`. lines.vo: This one is blocked. The board says for how long.

The card is rebuilt at legible weight and reads exactly what the real board reads: `T-5 — a reboot-surviving resume (launchd / systemd)` · `overnight-mode` · `agents: impl-reboot` · then the agent's own sentence, `the detached watcher does not survive a reboot, and I cannot verify a launchd plist without rebooting this machine` · and in clay, `no event 4 h`. The lane's 3px rail is clay. Sliding in beside it, the agent chip: `impl-reboot · implementer` / `3 HOURS since last signal — likely dead`. No alarm icon and no error triangle — the age is the alarm, and the board words it as an observation, not a verdict.

lines.vo: Halfway through, you remember something. So you say it.
lines.scene: The board is already live and already ticking; this beat interrupts it rather than introducing it. The camera pans back left to sit on BACKLOG and IN-PROGRESS. Your words type in over the lanes in the SANS face, gold #e8bc4d, unaligned to any grid, tilted, carrying a real drop shadow and a blinking caret: `also — rate-limit the webhook before we ship`. It must look like it does not belong on this page.

Two unrelated motions continue underneath: `#age-t6` steps `130 min`→`131 min`, and `#rail-inprogress` pulses opacity 0.6→1→0.6 once over 0.7s.

lines.vo: It does not land in the scrollback. It becomes a ticket.
lines.scene: The peak of the film, one continuous shot with no cut. A 3px gold segment runs along the board's top hairline and strikes the floating sentence. On contact the letterforms snap from sans to MONO and snap left onto the lane grid, and a card border DRAWS itself around them clockwise from the top-left corner. `T-9` types into the corner. Then gravity applies: the card drops into BACKLOG with one bounce, the lane header ticks (1) → (2), and the dim lifts off the board. Mechanical, not magical — a box being drawn around a sentence.
lines.animation: `#strike` (3px, --gold #d4a017) x 0→860px along the top hairline in 0.35s power2.in. On contact: `#aside` font-family swaps to var(--mono), rotation 2.5→0deg, text-align left, all inside 0.18s power4.out — landing exactly on the word 'ticket'. `#ticket-border` (SVG rect) stroke-dashoffset 640→0 clockwise in 0.45s power2.inOut. `#t9-id` types in 0.2s. `#aside` y -220px→0 in 0.5s back.out(1.7). `#lane-backlog` border-color --hairline→--brass-edge for 0.3s and back; `#hd-backlog` count tweens 1→2 snap:1; `#board-wrap` brightness 0.88→1 in 0.3s.

lines.vo: Queued as T nine. Written into the journal.
lines.scene: The receipt is the whole point of the beat. Under the top hairline one muted mono line fades up and fades on its own: `journal: ticket.declare T-9 · appended`. Beside the brass left rail, the run's own one-line confirmation in the product's own wording: `queued as T-9`. Then the new card is picked up immediately: its rail turns steel, `impl-webhook` types beneath the title, and the card slides one lane right into READY. slate.title: It Learns You
slate.purpose: The 9:16 short for the self-improvement loop — the pillar no competitor has. It makes the retro visible as a mechanism rather than a promise: the Stop gate that refuses one turn, the retro reading the record (never your mood), a shallow question edited out of the conductor's own instructions, three repeated requests hardening into a skill that must earn its context, a knowledge entry retired on its own counters, a candidate rejected by a named filter, and the 3-to-knowledge / 5-to-law ladder ending in a CLAUDE.md fence carrying the five dated entries that earned it. The spine is arithmetic the viewer can audit: the knowledge panel opens at 5 entries, drops to 4, climbs back to 5, and lands exactly where it began. That is "the more you use it, the better it gets" proved as restraint rather than accumulation. One destination: the sandbox board.

lines.vo: Every ticket merged. You close the session. It refuses.
lines.scene: COLD OPEN, no fade — the board is ALREADY live and ticking, rebuilt natively at board tokens (bg #1c1a16, hairline #332e27, --brass #a8863c, --steel #7d9ea9, --sage #88a06a, --clay #c07a70). Persistent five-tab bar across the top: `Overview · Board · Waiting on you (0) · Spend · Settings` — the queue reads zero because the work is finished. Header: `Tyran board · the-board · 7 of 7 tickets merged (100%)`. The DONE lane fills the frame with seven sage-railed cards carrying real titles (`T-5 — the waiting-on-you queue and the answer sheet`, `T-6 — a clickable sandbox published with the docs`). design.visualSpine: THE PANEL THAT DOES NOT GROW. The explainer's brass rail persists down the left edge of frame — the desk, never leaving — but this cut's own device is a number the viewer can audit: the knowledge panel's row counter. It is planted at `entries 5` during the read (04), deliberately does NOT move when a sentence is fixed rather than added (06), drops to 4 when a rule is retired on its own counters (10), climbs back to 5 when a signature graduates (12), and lands at 5 with `opened at 5` drawn beneath it (14). Every claim in the film is paid for in that counter, so 'the more you use it, the better it gets' is demonstrated as restraint rather than accumulation. The loop is made visible at three scales: the Stop gate refusing exactly once and immediately offering the decline, the cyan band reading the record before anything is written, and one card climbing three shelves. Nothing is ever shown being added without something being removed first — deletion is preferred to addition, and the frame enforces it.
motifs: THE COUNTER IS THE ARGUMENT — `entries 5 → 5 → 4 → 5`, ending exactly where it opened, with `opened at 5` printed beneath it in the landing frame. The anti-bloat claim is arithmetic on screen, not an adjective.

WORDS HARDEN INTO OBJECTS — human and prose input is sans, gold, unaligned, shadowed; machine state is mono, grid-aligned, bordered, flat. Every transition is a DRAWN border (stroke-dashoffset, clockwise from the top-left) plus a face swap landing on a beat, never a crossfade. It makes the skill card, the knowledge entry and the CLAUDE.md rule line rhyme as one gesture.

LIGHT READS, IT DOES NOT WRITE — cyan #8fd8ea appears only as the scan band moving over the journal column, and only while the retro is READING. The moment anything is written the cyan is gone and the frame is brass and sage. Cyan is never a border, a button or an accent.

ONE RECOIL, THEN RESOLVE — the Stop gate gets exactly one 0.12s hard recoil against the brass rail and one clay clause under a second, then immediately offers its own concession ('Deciding NOT to run one is a legitimate answer') with a `kind: skipped` receipt. The refusal never ends the beat, and it points at an unwritten record rather than at the operator.

STRIKE BEFORE DRAW — every addition is preceded by a removal in the same frame family: the struck sentence before the fixed one, the retired entry before the promoted one, the rejected candidate before the graduated one. A promotion without a visible rejection reads as bloat, which is the opposite of the claim.

THE GOLD LASH, GIVEN A MECHANISM — the hairline planted at frame one as the conductor rail gains exactly ONE new segment, at line 13, because a rule reaching law is the specific thing this retro added. The landing frame is a loop closing, not a logo appearing.

NOTHING FULLY STOPS — in every frame at least one true-to-product number is moving: an age chip stepping `3 min → 4 min → 5 min`, a lane count ticking, a counter digit-flipping, a bar finishing its draw. Every declared gap contains a visual event; the frozen final frame is banned and the tail is covered by two real board motions.

EVERY NUMBER KEEPS ITS RECEIPT — `7 of 7` · `3 asks` · `change 1 of at most 3` · `used 6 · helpful 0 · outdated 1` · `entries 5 / 4 / 5` · the thresholds 3 and 5 · the five dated MISTAKES.md entries (2026-05-02, 2026-06-11, 2026-07-03, 2026-07-28, 2026-08-09) · `K-07`, `K-12`, `worktree-missing-deps`. Every value exists in this repo. No invented figure, no savings percentage, no model name anywhere on screen or in the read.

critique:
## 1. Weakest pillar, and the one line that fixes it

**Weakest: "Agents are fully stateful. They retain memories. They retain the progress. They communicate with each other. They can see the status of the tasks."**

Across 82 beats in five cuts, agent‑to‑agent state appears exactly twice, both as scenery: a drawn file path (`.tyran/state/<init>/journal.jsonl · committed to your repo`) and a handoff stub (`ticket T-7 · files: scripts/cost.mjs, docs/cost.md`). Nothing ever *reads* either one. No cut shows a second agent starting from what a first agent wrote, and no cut shows a run surviving a restart or a compaction — which is the README's own lead paragraph ("a restart, a compaction and a colleague on another branch all read the same thing") and the thing every competitor table row in the repo is built on. The onboarding cut drops even the one clause the explainer has.

The line to change is **explainer [07-implementers]**:

> "Implementers take one story each. Own branch, empty scrollback. The agents forget. The team doesn't."

Four fragments, and the mechanism is in none of them. Replace with:

> **"Implementers take one story each, on their own branch, with an empty scrollback. What they find goes into the journal in your repo — so the reviewer starts already knowing it, and a crash or a compaction changes nothing."**

And change the shot to earn it: the journal path is already drawn along the bottom. Make the reviewer card in [08] open with its first line already populated — `from impl-T7 · finding F-12 · scripts/cost.mjs dedupes on requestId` — typed from the same string the implementer's panel wrote nine seconds earlier. That is one new tween, no new asset, and it converts a drawn file path into a visible channel. Mirror it in onboarding [12].

## 2. Lines that will read wrong aloud

**"In the same chat, it judged an auth boundary."** (explainer 01; also mistake [auth]). `auth` is a spelling, not a word; Gemini renders it inconsistently ("awth" / "oth"). → **"In the same chat, it judged an authentication boundary."** Keep `api/session.ts` and the literal `auth` on screen.

**"You didn't install a tool. You hired a manager. He runs the team. You only talk to him."** (explainer 03). Four terminal stops in one line is exactly the pause complaint. → **"You didn't install a tool — you hired a manager. He runs the team; you only talk to him."**

**"Security review always gets the strongest tier. No flag can drop it. No cost setting either."** (explainer 10). The third fragment is an afterthought and lands flat. → **"Security review always gets the strongest tier — and no flag or cost setting can lower it."**

**"Fifty-five percent of those were the manager's own context. It gets its own row, so nothing hides."** (explainer 17). Spoken, "it" has three possible antecedents. → **"Fifty-five percent of those tokens were the manager's own context. The manager gets its own row, so nothing hides inside the total."**

**"That was one request. You made two calls."** (explainer 25). "Calls" in a film about API spend is a landmine. → **"That was one request. You made two decisions. The team did the rest."**

**"None of this is a prompt asking nicely. A hook decides, before the tool runs."** (explainer 19). That comma is a 300 ms hole. → **"None of this is a prompt asking nicely. A hook decides before the tool ever runs."**

**"Chapter one." / "Chapter two." …** (onboarding 03, 05, 08, 13, 17, 21, 23 — seven spoken chapter announcements). The drawn chapter card and the eight‑row index already carry the number; the spoken version adds seven sentence‑final stops to a tutorial the operator already said pauses too much. Keep it on **01 and 08 only**; delete the words elsewhere. Recovers roughly 7–8 seconds and seven dead beats.

**"It reads how the repo is really worked. Not how a README describes it."** (onboarding 05). "README" is a coin flip between "read‑me" and "R‑E‑A‑D‑M‑E". → **"It reads how the repo is really worked, not how the docs describe it."**

**"One command, and this is the one place a Node version matters."** (onboarding 13). Vague spoken, and it never says the version. → **"One command — and it is the only place you need Node twenty-two."**

**"Install gitleaks first, or that gate has nothing to scan with."** (onboarding 22). → **"That gate scans with gitleaks. Install it, or there is nothing doing the scanning."**

**"The same failure three times becomes knowledge, in every handoff."** (retro 12). The trailing clause is not a sentence. → **"The same failure three times becomes knowledge — pasted into every handoff that touches those files."**

**"He interviews you first. At most four questions, each with his recommendation."** (explainer 04). `skills/run/SKILL.md:111` says *"at most 4 at once"* — a batch ceiling, not a total. → **"He interviews you first — batches of at most four, each with his recommendation."**

**"Then the bill. Four and a half million tokens. Four hundred and four requests."** (explainer 16). Two number fragments back to back read as a list. → **"Then the bill. Four and a half million tokens, across four hundred and four requests."**

## 3. Animations too vague to build, with the concrete version

**Explainer [02-diagnosis]** — scene says "the panel is suddenly small and alone"; anim says `scale 1.0→0.92 over 2.2s`. An 8% shrink over 2.2 s is imperceptible; the scene and the anim describe different shots. Concrete: `#stage-one` scale 1→0.58, y 0→+70px, 1.6 s sine.inOut, with a vignette `#frame-dark` opacity 0→0.5 over the same 1.6 s. The mistake cut already gets this right (`scale 1.0->0.86 and y 0->+50px`); copy it.

**Explainer [09-routing]** — "LIGHT IS THE BILL: the Tyran half is visibly darker." As specified it is *not* darker. Integrate the stated opacities over the shot: left = 0.95 × 8 s = 7.6 lamp‑seconds; right = cheap 0.28×8 + work ≈0.40×8 + deep 0.70×1.5 + top 0.90×0.9 ≈ **7.3**. Four dim lamps sum to the same light as one bright one, and the shot refutes its own thesis. Concrete: on the right, **only one lamp is above 0.10 at any instant** (idle level 0.06), giving ≈2.6 lamp‑seconds, and add an acceptance test the build can run: sample mean luminance of each half in the composited frame at 6 fixed times; require `right ≤ 0.45 × left` at every sample.

**Explainer [09] "Over the next 8 compressed seconds"** — the shot's duration is not free; it equals measured audio for that line (~6.5 s) plus gap. Specify the cycle in **proportions of the shot**, not seconds: cheap lit for 100%, work 8 pulses evenly spaced, deep 3 flares totalling 22%, top 2 flares totalling 11%. Same defect in [18-three-cents] ("holds 1.6s") and board [12] ("Hold 1.4s") — state them as fractions of the measured line.

**Board [03]** — `#lanes x 0 → -1980px` across ten lanes, while board [02] moves a card `x 0→341px` for "one lane width". Both cannot be true: ten lanes at 341 px pitch is 3410 px, so 1980 px stops with ~350 px of the DONE lane still off‑frame — and DONE(8) is the payoff of the pan. Concrete: pitch 341, left inset 24, frame 1080 → **pan to x = -(3410 + 24 - 1080) = -2354px**, and place the ten header colour tweens at `t_i = 2.9 × (24 + 341i + 170 - 540) / 2354`.

**Board [02]/[07]/[08] and explainer [12] — lane direction is backwards.** `LANES` in `scripts/project.mjs:646` is strongest‑verdict‑first: `waiting-operator, paused-limit, blocked, changes-requested, in-review, in-progress, ready, backlog, parked, done`.
